text: {"overall_winner":"B","qualities":[{"evidence":"clear opening claim: \"No, driverless cars should not be developed\"","quality":"thesis clarity","description":"The essay states a direct position immediately, so the reader knows exactly what it is arguing from the start."},{"evidence":"three body paragraphs on danger, lawsuits, and laziness","quality":"organization","description":"The essay develops its case in separate points, which makes the argument easier to follow than a mostly unstructured response."},{"evidence":"uses article details like \"sensors on the wheels\" and the driver being watched","quality":"source-based support","description":"It brings in specific evidence from the article to back up its claims instead of relying only on unsupported opinion."},{"evidence":"explains \"law suits, companies losing business, and people mad at companies\"","quality":"reasoning","description":"The essay tries to show consequences of driverless cars, not just list claims, which gives the argument more development."},{"evidence":"concludes with \"we should just stick to regular cars\"","quality":"conclusion","description":"It ends by restating the position and wrapping up the argument in a recognizable closing paragraph."}]}
